hero.title: A kernel. An opinion.
hero.lead: Studio runs AI agent pipelines via YAML configuration. Open source, declarative, retry-driven. It's voluntary.

thesis.title: What if agent orchestration was configuration, not code?
thesis.lead: Three premises shared with other frameworks. Three inverted by Studio.
thesis.card1_title: A pipeline is a YAML file
thesis.card1_body: Declares stages and groups. Each stage references an agent (runtime config) and a contract (JSON schema + constraints). Modifiable without a programming environment, line by line.
thesis.card2_title: The engine executes via the RALPH loop
thesis.card2_body: Execute → validate → advance if contract passes, retry with enriched feedback if it fails. No stage advances until its contract is met.
thesis.card3_title: Run it 10 times, get 10 correct outputs
thesis.card3_body: That's why contracts and retries exist. Anti-theatre by construction — the agent cannot skip steps that the contract requires.

tradeoffs.lead: LangGraph, CrewAI, Autogen share one premise: agent orchestration is code. Studio takes the inverse premise and assumes it.
tradeoffs.note: If your need fits the first three, no need to write Studio. If it doesn't, you write a YAML file reviewable line by line, modifiable without programming environment.

patterns.title: Three patterns.
patterns.lead: Everything is declarative. You describe what you want in YAML, the engine handles orchestration. Wiki Creator and Little Chef rely on it in production.
patterns.p1_body: One stage produces, another critiques. If the critic rejects, the group restarts with accumulated feedback. Max N iterations. Anti-theatre applied to creativity.
patterns.p2_body: Fan-out / fan-in declared in YAML. Stages run concurrently. The engine handles async/await and merge.
patterns.p3_body: The runner tracks tool calls. If the contract requires repo_manager.write_file minimum 1 and the agent calls none, the stage fails. Anti-theatre.

architecture.title: Seven packages, one monorepo.
architecture.title_accent: Each fits in a context window.
architecture.lead: The dependency graph is the architecture.
architecture.anonymizer_desc: PII detection & anonymization before LLM calls.
architecture.runner_desc: LLM calls, tool plugin runtime, multi-provider.
architecture.aside_ralph_body: Execute, validate, retry. Pass advances. Fail retries with enriched feedback.
architecture.aside_kernel_body: The kernel is the politics. Layers that don't know each other. Contracts as the only permitted dependency.

products.title: Two domains. Zero orchestration code.
products.wiki_desc: Extract entities, relations, generate wiki pages from EPUB books. NLP + LLM pipelines.
products.chef_desc: Meal planner. Researches cuisines, develops recipes with nutritional profile, generates grocery lists.

commons.left_body: Studio could have been a startup. The product shape lends itself to it. The opposite choice is deliberate. An AI agent orchestration kernel, captured by a company, becomes the bottleneck of everything flowing through it. Studio is designed so that it cannot be captured.
commons.mech1_body: Any modification used in production must be published under the same license.
commons.mech2_body: The kernel is intended to be owned by a non-profit, non-transferable foundation. The founder's progressive withdrawal is an explicit goal.
commons.mech3_body: Open source kernel (commons) · Support core (hosting, maintenance) · Products powered by Studio (commercial or open source). No commercial entity has authority over the kernel.
commons.quote_after: by design. The license is the mechanism that maintains it.

install.meta_title: Install Studio — Quick start in 4 steps
install.meta_description: Install the Studio CLI, create a project, configure a provider, and run your first pipeline in under 5 minutes.
install.title: Get running in minutes.
install.lead: Install the CLI, create a project, wire a provider, run a pipeline.
install.beta_banner: Studio is in active beta. Expect bugs and breaking changes.
install.step1_desc: Requires Node.js 18+. Installs the global `studio` command.
install.step2_desc: Scaffolds a project with the `software-full` template. The pipeline, contracts, agents and tools are ready to run.
install.step3_desc: Set your Anthropic API key. Other providers (OpenAI, Mistral) follow the same pattern.
install.step4_desc: Replace the input with your feature description. Studio validates every stage output against its contract.
install.next1_body: Edit stages, agents, and contracts in YAML. The template is a starting point, not a constraint.
install.next2_body: A .tool.yaml file is all you need. Define the command, parameters, and description. No code required.
install.next3_body: Seven packages, strict dependency order. The engine knows nothing about your domain — that's the design.

contribute.meta_title: Contribute to Studio — Open source, AGPL-3.0
contribute.meta_description: Studio is in active beta. Bug reports, PRs, and tool plugins are all welcome. Here's how to get started.
contribute.title: Studio is open.
contribute.lead: Studio is in active beta. Issues, PRs, and tool plugins are welcome. The kernel is a commons — every contribution shapes what stays open.
contribute.how_issue_body: Bug, question, or proposal — open an issue on GitHub. No template required. Be specific about what you observed vs. what you expected.
contribute.how_pr_body: Fork the repo, create a branch, use conventional commits. Run `pnpm build` before pushing — CI will reject a broken build.
contribute.how_tool_body: A tool plugin is a `.tool.yaml` file. No code required. Define the command name, description, and parameters. The engine calls it.
contribute.know_invariants_body: Seven packages with a strict dependency order. No inversions. The kernel knows nothing about your domain — that's the point.
contribute.know_kernel_body: The engine has no concept of code, files, or any specific domain. All domain logic comes from YAML configs. This is not a constraint — it's the design.
contribute.know_license_body: Any modification used in production must be published under the same license. If that doesn't fit your use case, Studio is probably not the right tool.
contribute.priority1_body: Studio is in beta. The seven packages work, but edge cases surface with real-world use. Bug reports from active users are the most valuable contributions right now.
contribute.priority2_body: The software-full template is complete and validated. Other templates — finance, data, deeper analysis variants — are scaffolded but need real-world validation.
contribute.priority3_body: Studio Community hosts contributed tool plugins and custom templates. The registry is live but the ecosystem is just starting.
contribute.closing_body: Governance, non-profit foundation, and the three structural mechanisms that keep the kernel a commons.

meta.title: Studio Foundation — Agentic pipeline orchestrator
meta.description: Studio is a domain-agnostic agentic pipeline orchestrator. Execute multi-stage LLM workflows with strict output validation and automatic retry.

mission.meta_description: Studio is an explicitly political project. Open source by structural choice, domain-agnostic by commitment, provider-agnostic by commitment, anti-capture by design.
mission.hero_lead: Seven positions. Open source, domain-agnostic, provider-agnostic, anti-capture. The kernel is a commons.
mission.s1_p1: The productivity gains from AI are real. Left unchecked, they follow the same pattern as every previous wave of automation. Value concentrates at the top. Tools become proprietary. The people who need them most get priced out.
mission.s1_p2: Studio exists to make that harder to do.
mission.s2_p1: The AGPL-3.0 license is not a default. It is a deliberate mechanism against capture.
mission.s2_p2: The kernel is a commons. Anyone can use it, extend it, build commercial products on it. If you modify Studio itself and run the modified version as a network service, you publish your changes. This prevents cloud providers from taking the engine, closing it, and selling it back.
mission.s2_p3: This is not anti-commercial. Build whatever you want on top. Sell it. The license protects the foundation, not the products built on it.
mission.s3_p1: The engine has zero knowledge of what domain it operates in. It doesn't know what "code" or "transactions" or "medical records" mean. All domain semantics come from YAML configs.
mission.s3_p2: This is not a feature, it is an architectural commitment that prevents any single use case from claiming ownership of the kernel. The engine belongs to everyone precisely because it serves no one domain specifically.
mission.s4_p1: Anthropic, OpenAI, or any other provider, swappable per agent, per stage, per pipeline. The orchestration layer depends on the work being done correctly, not on who does it.
mission.s4_p2: No vendor lock-in. No preferred provider. The runtime is neutral infrastructure.
mission.s5_p1: Ideological drift rarely happens through open conflict. It happens through accumulation of "reasonable" decisions: a proprietary integration here, a vendor dependency there, a governance exception that becomes precedent.
mission.s5_p2: Studio integrates mechanisms for deceleration, traceability, and veto. Any evolution that improves performance at the cost of increasing inequality is a regression, not progress.
mission.s6_p1: Decision-making power is held primarily by the people directly affected by the inequalities the project aims to reduce. Diversity is not symbolic, it is decisional.
mission.s6_p2: The full governance model and foundational principles are documented in the charter.
mission.s7_p1: Reduce the cost of building software and automating complex work to the point where a single person can create and operate products that generate real value. Not by coding everything themselves, but by orchestrating AI agents with structural guarantees of quality.
mission.s7_quote: The kernel is free. The agents are interchangeable. The configs belong to whoever writes them.

charter.meta_title: Charter — What Studio is, what it isn't, and how it's governed
charter.meta_description: Studio's charter describes what it is, what it is not, and how it is governed. A reference document for contributors, users, and anyone wondering why Studio is structured the way it is.
charter.hero_title: What Studio is, what it isn't, and how it's governed.
charter.hero_lead: A reference document for contributors, users, and anyone wondering why Studio is structured the way it is.
charter.s1_p1: Studio is an orchestration system for AI agent pipelines. Technical work happens through declarative YAML configuration, validated by contracts, retried by a RALPH loop. The kernel knows nothing about the domain. All business content lives in configs.
charter.s1_p2: Studio is designed on the model of git: a tool you install globally, that lives in a .studio/ folder inside the user's project, that you use daily from the terminal. Not a framework to learn. Not a platform to join. A dev tool.
charter.s2_not1: Studio is not an AI agent. Agents are secondary, interchangeable, fallible.
charter.s2_not2: Studio is not a framework. You don't inherit from a class, you don't implement an interface, you don't learn a DSL. You write YAML.
charter.s2_not3: Studio is not a platform. The kernel is open source, the hosted API (when it exists) will be optional, content stays in your repo.
charter.s2_not4: Studio is not a commercial product. The kernel is and will remain a commons.
charter.s3_intro: Studio is a project explicitly anchored on the left. This mention is not a slogan added to a neutral product, it is the foundation of the project itself. Three principles structure technical and organizational decisions:
charter.s3_p1_body: Tools do not serve everyone the same way. Studio is designed with first thought for people for whom current tooling is inadequate: neurodivergent people, precarious people, people excluded from centers of technical power.
charter.s3_p2_body: The productivity gains that AI makes possible currently concentrate value at the top. Studio exists to make agent orchestration accessible without depending on a proprietary platform that captures the value produced.
charter.s3_p3_body: The project is designed to last, not to scale. Human pace takes precedence over the roadmap. The founder can step back without the system collapsing.
charter.s3_close: Ideological neutrality is neither sought nor claimed.
charter.s4_title: Why a commons, not a startup
charter.s4_intro: Studio could have been a startup. The product shape lends itself to it, the market exists, demand is rising. The opposite choice is deliberate: an AI agent orchestration kernel, captured by a company, becomes the bottleneck of everything that flows through it. Studio is designed so that it cannot be captured.
charter.s4_sub: Three structural mechanisms ensure this non-capture.
charter.s4_mech1_body: Any modification of Studio used in production must be published under the same license. A company that forks Studio for internal proprietary use violates the license. This is the strategy the GNU project used to prevent commercial capture of free software, and it is deliberate.
charter.s4_mech2_title: Mechanism 2: Ownership by a non-profit foundation
charter.s4_mech2_body: The kernel is intended to be owned by a non-profit, non-transferable foundation. The foundation bears the name of its founder as recognition of the initiative, without implying permanent or exclusive authority. The progressive withdrawal of the founder is part of the explicit goals of the project.
charter.s4_mech2_body2: The foundation's governance is designed to give decision-making power to the people directly affected by the inequalities the project seeks to reduce. Diversity is not symbolic, it is decision-making.
charter.s4_mech3_intro: Studio is structured in three layers whose authorities are watertight:
charter.s4_layer1_body: Commons. Non-transferable. Governed by constitutional invariants. Final authority on technical decisions.
charter.s4_layer2_body: Hosting, maintenance, documentation. Generates revenue subordinated to the commons. On the model of the Linux Foundation which funds Linux without controlling it.
charter.s4_layer3_body: Applications built from templates. Can be open source or commercial. Can appear or disappear. Exercise no power over the kernel.
charter.s4_close: As GitHub, GitLab, and Bitbucket are to git: products built on a free tool without authority over it.
charter.s5_intro: Studio is a monorepo of seven packages, plus a template system.
charter.s5_concepts: Five concepts differentiate Studio from other orchestrators:
charter.s5_c1_body: Execute, validate against the contract, retry with enriched feedback if fail, repeat until success or max attempts. This is what makes pipelines reliable. No stage advances until its output respects its contract.
charter.s5_c2_body: Structural validation schemas. Validation is binary, pass or fail. No gray zone, no configurable acceptance score.
charter.s5_c3_body: Detection of agents that pretend to have done the work without having done it. If a contract requires tool calls and the agent made none, the stage fails regardless of the quality of the text produced.
charter.s5_c4_body: Multi-stage feedback loops. Creation, critique, revision automatic, without human intervention between iterations.
charter.s5_c5_body: .tool.yaml files that define capabilities for agents. Self-documenting, project-scoped, double-gated. Creating a tool requires no code.
charter.s5_invariants: Six architectural invariants ensure the system remains coherent:
charter.s5_inv1: The engine is domain-agnostic. All domain comes from YAML.
charter.s5_inv2: ralph does not know runner. The executor is generic.
charter.s5_inv3: runner does not validate, does not retry. That is ralph's job.
charter.s5_inv4: contracts is a leaf package. Zero internal dependencies.
charter.s5_inv5: Tools are in runner, not in engine.
charter.s5_inv6: Prompts are in runner, not in engine.
charter.s5_close: If a feature can be configured in YAML rather than coded, it is in YAML. This is not a stylistic preference, it is a constitutional rule of the kernel.
charter.s6_p1: Templates are not finished products. They are architectural patterns that generate complete applications, like create-react-app or create-next-app, but for AI-orchestrated apps.

s6_templates.t1: software-full — Software development, full pipeline with QA review
s6_templates.t2: software — Code generation with repo, shell and search tools
s6_templates.t3: content — Content creation and editing with search
s6_templates.t4: document-analysis — Document extraction and structured analysis
s6_templates.t5: parallel-tasks — Fan-out parallel task execution with consolidation

charter.s6_p3: A template generates a functional out-of-the-box app: base pipelines for the domain, adapted tools (.tool.yaml), configured contracts and agents, starter DB schema (Prisma), minimal but functional application code.
charter.s6_p4: Templates are designed to be reusable. Several products can start from the same template and diverge completely: Wiki Creator and Voice Training both use the analysis/ template, but one analyzes books and the other processes voice. It's the architectural pattern that is shared, not the domain.
charter.s6_registry: Eventually, a community registry will allow publishing and installing custom templates. But this phase comes after validation of the official templates by real products.
charter.s7_intro: Inspired by the Linus Torvalds model: the tool is free, the ecosystem funds the development.
charter.s7_item1: The kernel is free, open source, forever
charter.s7_item2: The official templates are free, open source
charter.s7_item3: The hosted API (Studio Cloud, future) generates revenue via subscriptions
charter.s7_item4: Specialized products can be commercial or open source according to each team's choices
charter.s7_item5: The foundation is funded by the ecosystem of companies that depend on Studio
charter.s7_close: Linus never sold Linux or git. He is funded by the companies that depend on them, through the Linux Foundation. Studio follows the same model. No commercial decision can take precedence over the kernel invariants. Any evolution that improves performance or monetization at the cost of worsening inequalities is considered a regression.
charter.s8_intro: The kernel is treated as a constitution, not as an implementation. Final authority over structural decisions belongs to the kernel and the foundation, not to agents, commercial products, or individual contributors.
charter.s8_p1_body: Not-acting is a valid decision. A feature that could be done does not have to be done.
charter.s8_p2_body: They execute, they do not govern.
charter.s8_p3_body: Structural choices are documented (Architecture Decision Records). A decision without trace did not happen.
charter.s8_p4_body: Any evolution can be blocked if it compromises the political anchoring of the project, even if it improves performance.
charter.s8_p5_body: Governance decisions go in priority to the people the project seeks to serve, not to contributors with the most commits.
charter.s9_item1: A single public product at a time
charter.s9_item3: Any new idea passes through a latency period
charter.s9_item4: Human pace takes precedence over the roadmap
charter.s9_item5: Templates are created only after validation by a real product
charter.s9_close: Studio is not designed to scale fast. It is designed to last.
charter.s10_item1: The kernel remains coherent over time
charter.s10_item2: Projects finish or stop explicitly, they do not die by abandonment
charter.s10_item3: The cognitive load of the founder and contributors decreases over time
charter.s10_item6: The founder can step back without system collapse
charter.s10_item7: Templates are reused by the community
charter.s10_item8: Several products live on the same template
charter.s10_close: Money is a means of sustainability, never an end.
charter.s11_intro: Studio is in active development. Three ways to participate now:
charter.s11_c1_body: The repo welcomes questions, bug reports, improvement proposals, usage feedback. Topics that might interest others go on GitHub, the rest by email.
charter.s11_c2_body: PRs are welcome, respecting the architectural invariants. See CONTRIBUTING.md for details.
charter.s11_c3_body: .tool.yaml files are the main extension point of Studio. If you build a tool useful to others, it can be published in the community registry when it opens.
charter.s12_p1: Studio is in pre-launch. No public promotion yet. No hosted API yet. No version 1.0 yet.
charter.s12_p2: Once Code Builder is validated in production, Studio will move into "first public release" mode. Until then, interested users can follow the repo and test locally. Bugs and incompatibilities are expected.
charter.quote_final: Nothing in this document is for sale.
